title: 3D Navigation, UCS/Workplanes & Modeling: the bounded professional 3D environment
objective: Deliver the professional 3D modeling/navigation environment on the frozen CAD/BIM Product Architecture v1.0 (Issue #90; the CAD-PARITY program's next subsystem after CAD-PARITY-008 verified at 9320311): deterministic 3D navigation (orbit/pan/zoom/fit-extents, the six standard views + isometric, orthographic and perspective camera modes with deterministic camera state persisted as non-versioned editor settings — view state strictly separated from model history, a view-cube/navigation-surface data model shared by both hosts, deterministic 3D selection through the shared projection math with exact ordered hit lists), the UCS/workplane subsystem (the implicit World UCS plus user-named UCS definitions with origin + orthonormal axes as a versioned document table, activation/current-workplane semantics as non-versioned editor state, deterministic world↔UCS↔screen transforms with exact inverses, UCS-aware numeric input for the modeling commands, grid/snap projection onto the active workplane, typed rejections for degenerate/non-orthonormal configurations), bounded 3D modeling (solid primitive creation — box/cylinder/extrusion-derived solids — through the EXISTING OCCT adapter boundary with engine IDs as provenance only, UCS-aware 3D MOVE/ROTATE/SCALE as atomic revisions with exact inverses, deterministic 3D selection at element granularity with typed declines for face/edge/vertex sub-entity picking that the engine boundary cannot yet support deterministically, a section/slice PREVIEW foundation — section-plane definitions as versioned document content plus a deterministic bounded plane∩bbox intersection preview with a typed decline for exact BRep cross-sections), the shared command vocabulary and App API surface, professional 3D viewport surfaces on Web and Electron sharing the same semantic contracts/transforms/selection (LOCK-004), save/open/undo/redo/replay persistence with Construction Graph mapping by canonical identity, and Vercel deployed verification of the exact implementation head including the real 3D workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic 3D navigation through the shared pure camera/projection modules consumed by both hosts and the App API: orbit/pan/zoom/fit-extents, the standard views and isometric preset, orthographic/perspective modes, with the camera state persisted as non-versioned editor settings (save/open restores it; it never enters the revision content hashes) and view state strictly separated from model history.

Real UCS/workplane semantics through the shared App API: the implicit World UCS (never removable) plus named UCS definitions as a versioned document table (create/rename/update/remove with exact inverses; duplicate names rejected; degenerate/non-orthonormal axis triples are typed declines), activation semantics as non-versioned editor state, world↔UCS↔screen transforms with exact inverses, UCS-aware numeric input in the modeling commands, and grid/snap projection onto the active workplane.

Representative 3D modeling workflow through the shared App API: box/cylinder/extrusion-derived solid creation placed through the ACTIVE UCS using the existing GeometryDescriptor vocabulary (transform-wrapped descriptors; no new engine ops), each creation is ONE atomic revision with the engine result (meshToken/bbox/provenance) persisted in the SAME revision, and UCS-aware MOVE/ROTATE/SCALE transform existing solids with exact inverses (undo/redo/replay integrity).

Deterministic 3D selection: element-granularity picking through the shared projection/ray math with an exactly-ordered hit list (distance then canonical id — no tie ambiguity), and typed declines for face/edge/vertex sub-entity selection (the engine boundary exposes no topology mapping — never a silent approximation).

Web and Electron execute the same semantic command stream and produce equivalent persisted model state, canonical identity mappings and camera/UCS state (the shared parity fixture); both hosts render the 3D viewport from the SAME shared camera/projection modules (no host-local navigation math).

The OCCT geometry engine remains strictly behind the EngineAdapterBundle/worker boundary: no engine imports in renderer/workspace/CADDocument/App-API domain modules (the LOCK-018 no-forbidden-imports scan stays green); engine ids are provenance only.

Unsupported 3D operations fail explicitly and deterministically: sub-entity selection, exact BRep cross-sections, non-planar workplanes and degenerate UCS configurations are typed declines with clear reasons — no silent approximations.
Existing CAD-PARITY-002..008 parity fixtures and regression suites remain green and byte-identical (additive-optional snapshot/history fields; the canonical-minimal contract).

Save/open and replay preserve UCS/workplane definitions, section-plane definitions, solid elements with their engine provenance, camera/UCS editor state, and history integrity (immutable revisions, exact inverses, deterministic replay).

The exact implementation head is deployed and browser-verified on Vercel with the real 3D workflow (navigation state, UCS switching, solid creation, transforms, selection) reproducing the pinned parity fixture byte-identically; governance evidence binds tests, CI, the deployed revision and review state to exact commits and timestamps.
non_goals: Full AutoCAD 3D feature parity in one work item (the bounded slice only).
Advanced surface modeling, subdivision meshes, point clouds, or large-model performance optimization (reserved for later work items).
Full mesh editing and arbitrary face-level topology editing (sub-entity selection is a typed decline in this slice).
Exact BRep cross-section computation (the section/slice surface is the bounded plane∩bbox preview foundation + a typed decline for exact sections — a later slice at the adapter boundary).
Full visual styles/rendering pipeline parity (deterministic flat-shaded wireframe visuals only — no materials, lights beyond the fixed deterministic light, or photorealism).

Advanced solids history/direct modeling beyond the existing verified kernel and adapter capabilities (no new OCCT worker operations — the slice composes the EXISTING box/cylinder/extrude/transform/fuse/cut descriptor vocabulary).
Architecture changes (ConstructionOS Architecture v1.1 and CAD/BIM Product Architecture v1.0 stay frozen).
risk_assumptions: ASSUMPTION (mesh availability for the 3D viewport): the hosts render solids from the persisted meshToken via the adapter's MeshProvider capability; when the engine provides no mesh (the dummy adapter in tests) the viewport renders the persisted bbox wireframe, labeled as such — never an approximation presented as exact.

ASSUMPTION (SVG/canvas projection rendering): the 3D viewport is a deterministic SVG/canvas projection surface (the COMPAT-CAD-002 BIM viewport precedent — explicitly no WebGL/three.js/npm additions in this slice).

RISK (floating-point determinism across hosts): the shared projection math is IEEE-754 with a documented fixed operation order and canonical formatting; the parity fixture pins the rendered-scene canonical hash so any host divergence is caught byte-exactly.

ASSUMPTION (perspective projection scope): the perspective mode is a bounded standard pinhole projection with a fixed field-of-vocabulary (fov in degrees) used for rendering and picking; no lens distortion or camera calibration vocabulary.
evidence_requirements: Deterministic automated suites for the 3D core (camera orbit/pan/zoom/fit + the standard views, the orthographic/perspective projection with exact screen math and inverses, the view-cube face model), the UCS/workplane model (orthonormality validation + typed declines, world↔UCS↔screen transform exact inverses, grid/snap projection), the deterministic selection (ray math, exactly-ordered hit lists, typed sub-entity declines) and the section preview foundation (plane∩bbox, canonical preview hash, typed exact-section decline).

Document-model suites: ucs-/sp-minting, the new edit variants with exact inverses incl. key-adding updates, canonical-minimal snapshot/history with legacy byte-identity (all six existing fixtures), replay integrity, reference-checked removals and the command-layer rules (active-UCS removal decline, World immutability).

App-API/command suites over the reference adapter (deterministic analytic geometry) with real-OCCT coverage in CI (the engine-availability pattern): the full command vocabulary incl. UCS-aware numeric input, atomic revisions with engine provenance persisted, undo/redo/replay round trips, and the parity anchor hash.

Web-host smoke against the dev server asserting the pinned fixture byte-identically (save hash, command stream, 3D scene canonical SVG hash) and the Electron-host smoke over the REAL UI asserting the same fixture — Web/Electron semantic parity.

Deployed verification: the exact implementation head deployed to Vercel, browser-verified with the six legacy fixtures byte-identical AND the new 3D fixture byte-identical against the deployment, with deployment id + commit + timestamp bound on the PR.

evidence.description: PR #92 ARCHITECT-REVIEW REMEDIATION (CHANGES REQUESTED — the perspective fit): the review found fitCameraToBBox()'s perspective distance max(halfY, halfX/aspect, halfZ)/sin(fov/2)·FIT_MARGIN to be an axis-extent heuristic that does not guarantee all eight corners inside the perspective frustum for oblique directions (measured on the pre-fix head: the isometric fit of the 10-cube put 4/8 corners OUTSIDE an 800×600 fov-60 viewport at screen x −52.9/852.9; even the front-view fit failed 4/8 — the prior suite only asserted corners stay in front of the eye plane, never inside the viewport). FIXED in a87b642 with the EXACT per-corner solve: each corner offset v (kept eye-direction frame, right/up ⊥ dir) has camera-plane coordinates (xc, yc, zc) = (v·right, v·up, d − v·dir) and the pinhole viewport bound |xc| ≤ zc·aspect·tan(fovY/2) ∧ |yc| ≤ zc·tan(fovY/2) is LINEAR in d (d ≥ |v·right|/(aspect·tan(fovY/2)) + v·dir ∧ d ≥ |v·up|/tan(fovY/2) + v·dir); the max over all 8 corners is the minimal sufficient distance for ARBITRARY camera direction/aspect/fov, ×FIT_MARGIN keeps the documented 10% margin and every corner strictly in front of the eye plane. Adversarially verified before landing: 160,000 corner projections over 20,000 randomized configurations (fov 1–178°, aspect 0.2–5.2, arbitrary orientations incl. rolled up hints, non-cubic and flat boxes) — ZERO failures. NEW regression tests (the review's required list, model3d core 35 → 38 tests, the P009 suite 61 → 64): the isometric perspective fit (the exact closed-form distance (10√2 + 5/√3)·FIT_MARGIN + all-corners-inside across 8 aspect/fov configurations), strongly non-cubic boxes (40×4×6 slab, 2×2×30 column, 25×1×1 beam, 10×10×0 plane) × 7 directions × 3 viewports, arbitrary orientation + rolled up hint + narrow fov 15° + extreme aspects 0.25/4, and the explicit assertAllCornersInsideViewport() on EVERY case incl. the upgraded front-view fit and the perspective empty-box unit fallback. FIXTURES PRESERVED BYTE-IDENTICALLY (the fix is perspective-only; the parity fixture runs orthographic): the PARITY ANCHOR unchanged (save b8cf24a22da9ca62…, svg 6fc199e61f7c827a…, section 2955ff1d95c57a71…), the Web model3d smoke 26/26 PASS and the Electron real-UI smoke 32/32 PASS both MATCHING the pinned fixture (save d2e7a95e…, scene SVG 629b2071…, section preview 2955ff1d…, echo digest 04d6d390…, the 26-command stream) on the remediated tree. evidence.description: PR #92 DEC-001 REMEDIATION (round 2 — the orthographic fit + the turntable orbit): FIXED at b72ed0e (app/src/workspace/model3d/camera.ts + the two test files ONLY — no architecture change, no fixture rewrite). (1) Orthographic fitCameraToBBox() now derives the half-height from the camera-frame projections of all 8 corners: H ≥ max over corners of max(|v·up|, |v·right|/aspect), ·FIT_MARGIN — the minimal sufficient bound for ARBITRARY direction/aspect AND roll (the frame's own right/up), degenerating to the previous max(halfY, halfX/aspect) arithmetic EXACTLY on the six axis views (float-op identical — the fixtures' axis-view fits are unchanged). decisions.rationale: Architect review of PR #92, round 2 — the review covered the remediation itself (the code), not just the reported test results; delivered through the implementation channel (no GitHub review object registered; the receipt anchor is the remediation session's environment start 2026-08-30T05:55:20Z — the review was complete on delivery). VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED (not approved, not merged). The round-1 perspective-fit remediation (a87b642, EV-005..007) was reviewed and confirmed CORRECT ('the remediation's perspective formula itself is sound'); the engine boundary, shared-core design, UCS model, deterministic picking and Web/Electron architectural direction remain consistent with Issue #90. TWO defects found. (1) Orthographic fitCameraToBBox() is still mathematically incorrect: the branch computed halfHeight = max(halfY, halfX/aspect)·FIT_MARGIN — world X/Y extents only. For an arbitrary/iso camera the viewport bounds are governed by the camera's right/up axes, so the world Z axis contributes to the projected height and width; measured on the review head, the isometric orthographic fit of the 10-cube produced projected Y coordinates −145.4→745.4 on an 800×600 viewport (2/8 corners outside) despite the function's documented all-eight-corners guarantee — directly inconsistent with the P009 acceptance criterion (the existing ortho tests only covered the front view where the world axes line up; the existing iso test checked the direction, not the corners). (2) orbitCamera() applies yaw to the eye vector and then pitch about the PRE-YAW camera right axis rather than the yaw-updated right axis — the Web viewport's normal combined drag orbitCamera(camera, dx·0.5°, dy·0.5°) therefore composes a different rotation than the documented turntable semantics for diagonal drags (measured: a 45°+30° drag from eye (10,0,0) landed 1.74 units off the exact turntable position); the tests exercised yaw and pitch essentially independently. The camera module claimed a stronger invariant than it implemented; fitCameraToBBox() must guarantee it in BOTH camera modes.
decisions.remediation_required: One bounded P009 fix round: (1) correct orthographic fitCameraToBBox() — derive the required screen-space half-width/half-height from the camera-frame projections of all 8 bbox corners, not world X/Y extents; (2) preserve the current eye direction and camera orientation; (3) add regression coverage for isometric orthographic fit, arbitrary oblique orthographic fit, strongly non-cubic boxes, rolled camera orientation, and an explicit assertion that all 8 corners are strictly inside the viewport; (4) correct orbitCamera() so combined yaw+pitch uses the proper turntable frame/order, with diagonal-drag regression tests; (5) re-run the full app suite, the P009 deterministic suite, the Web smoke, the Electron 3D smoke, all existing parity fixtures, CI and the exact-head Vercel deployment verification; (6) return PR #92 to PR_OPEN with fresh evidence bound to the actual final head — no architecture changes and no fixture rewrites unless demonstrably required.
